transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, what finally made me call the employee assistance program to set this up is that I’m barely sleeping right. I just lie there at night replaying work stuff and arguments from home. Then I end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and... I just start the day feeling like I never really rested at all.
Beyond the sleep problems, how has your mood been over the past few weeks? Have you been feeling sad, empty, or just not interested in things you normally enjoy?

Yeah, empty is probably a good word for it. Most days, I just have this... this heavy, gray mood. It's like it follows me everywhere, from the office to the car and back to the house. And it's not even like there's always a reason for it. Even when nothing specific is going on or going wrong, I just feel kind of hollow.
How long have you been experiencing this empty mood and sleep problems? Can you think back to when this all started?

It's been going on for a while now. I'd say... probably about a year and two months. That's right around the time the arguments at home started getting a lot worse. It just kind of started then and hasn't really let up since.

When the arguments at home got worse about a year ago, did your mood and sleep problems start right around that same time, or had you been feeling this empty and having trouble sleeping even before the relationship stress began?

I think it's hard to say for sure. Um... it all kind of blends together when I look back at it now. I don't think I was having the sleep issues or feeling quite this empty before the arguments got really bad, but... yeah, I can't be one hundred percent certain what came first. It really just feels like it all hit right around the same time.

On days when nothing particular is happening at work or at home, do you still find yourself feeling that empty, heavy mood and having trouble sleeping, or does it tend to get better on those quieter days?

Yeah, the quiet days don't really seem to make a difference. Even when things are totally fine at work or nobody is arguing at home, that heavy, empty feeling is still there. The sleep problems, too. It's like my mood doesn't really care if it's a good day or a bad day, it just kind of stays the same.
When you think about things you used to enjoy doing—hobbies, time with friends, activities like that—do you still find them enjoyable, or has that interest kind of faded away?

Yeah, that interest has definitely faded. I used to really look forward to doing things... you know, playing pickup basketball, bowling nights, going out to music festivals, or even just firing up the smoker for friends on the weekend. 

But lately, I just... I don't know, I don't really care about doing any of that. I end up canceling a lot of the time. And even when I do force myself to show up, it just feels like I'm going through the motions. I'm physically there, but I'm not actually enjoying myself anymore.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight over this past year or so?

Yeah, my appetite has definitely been off for months now. I usually just end up running on coffee all the way through lunch at work, and then... well, I mostly just pick at dinner with my family. I'm just not really hungry. But the weird thing is, even though I'm not eating much, I realized recently that my belt is sitting a notch tighter than it used to. So I guess I've actually put on a little weight somehow.

Over this past year, have you noticed any changes in how fast or slow you move or speak? For example, do you feel like you're moving in slow motion, or conversely, do you feel restless or like you need to keep moving?

I haven't really felt restless, it's more... slower, I guess. People at work probably wouldn't say I'm falling apart or anything, but I can definitely tell I move slower. 

I'll catch myself just sitting there staring at my laptop a lot longer than I used to. And sometimes, if one of my sales reps asks me a question—even a really simple one—it takes me a beat too long to answer them. It's just like it takes me an extra second to process things and actually get the words out.
Have you had any thoughts about wanting to hurt yourself or wishing you were dead?

I'm not... I don't have any sort of plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But, um, the thought does come up more than I really want to admit. Just... sometimes I think that maybe my family and everyone would be better off if I just didn't wake up one morning. It's just a thought that passes through, but it's there.

Have there been any times over the past year or so when you felt unusually energetic, optimistic, or like you could do a lot more than usual—maybe needing less sleep but still feeling rested, or feeling like your thoughts were racing?

No, not really. I've never had anything like that. I don't think I've felt unusually energetic or anything in a long time. It's mostly just been feeling tired and slow. I definitely haven't had racing thoughts or felt like I didn't need sleep. If anything, I just want to sleep more.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a major depressive episode characterized by persistent depressed mood (empty, heavy, gray mood), anhedonia (loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities), sleep disturbance (early morning awakening around 3-4 AM), appetite changes, psychomotor retardation, concentration difficulties, and passive suicidal ideation. While symptoms began around the time of increased marital conflict, the patient reports that the depressive symptoms persist independently of current stressors and have remained relatively stable over 14 months. The absence of manic/hypomanic episodes and the severity and duration of symptoms support a diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder, unspecified (F32.9). Adjustment Disorder with depressed mood (F43.21) is considered but less likely given the severity, persistence despite stress resolution, and the presence of multiple neurovegetative symptoms beyond what would be expected as a direct response to the identified stressor.
